clue.text: Most distinguished head in case

parts.note: nob is old slang for the head
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: The top person in a legal case or packing case is singled out as the most eminent.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of noble: the most aristocratic or eminent, so the most distinguished.

clue.text: Nothing in creed is well done

indicators.note: in means the zero goes inside the creed's name

parts.note: the Nicene Creed is a Christian statement of faith
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Having no faith at all is apparently an achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside NICENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice one is colloquial praise, an exclamation meaning good work.

clue.text: Live competition in which Liverpool play caused vexation

definitions.note: a past-tense verb phrase, matching the answer as the past form of beleaguer

parts.note: to be is to live, exist
a league is a sports competition
Liverpool football club play in red shirts

explanation.surface: A football league contest involving Liverpool caused upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool are an English football club who wear red.
explanation.definitionFit: To beleaguer is to harass or trouble persistently, so its past form means vexed someone.

clue.text: Book used curious game symbols inside

indicators.note: inside places the game marks within the rearranged letters
curious means odd, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: X and O are the symbols of noughts and crosses

explanation.surface: A book employed odd game symbols within its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' rearranges the letters to EDUS before 'inside' takes the marks. Noughts and crosses is the British name for tic-tac-toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Exodus is the second book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Land in tree: am picked up after major alarm sounded

indicators.note: after places the tree and reversed words following the spoken word
sounded means the word is spoken, giving a word of similar sound

parts.note: terror is extreme fear, major alarm
a fir is a tree

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the letters are lifted, read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Up a tree, someone is picked up after a big scare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounded' turns TERROR into TERRA by sound; 'picked up' reverses AM to MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is Latin for solid ground, dry land as opposed to sea or air.

clue.text: Ropy work, in which arm came loose

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters have come free and been set down in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A piece of knotted craftwork in which someone's arm worked itself free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges ARM CAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is decorative knotting of cord, a craft made of rope or string.

clue.text: In opera she sings only one note or two

indicators.note: or two means the note is given a second time

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An opera singer whose part consists of just a note or two.
explanation.walkthrough: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème.
explanation.definitionFit: The seamstress Mimi is the soprano heroine of a famous opera.

clue.text: Plan together to cheat father, keeping quiet

parts.note: to con is to cheat

indicators.note: keeping means the father's word holds the quiet sign within

parts.note: a sire is a father
P, piano, means quiet in music

explanation.surface: Scheming with others to swindle Dad while staying silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts P inside SIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot jointly, making secret plans with others.

clue.text: Remains no less hard

parts.note: as, as in as good as, means no less than
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Something stays just as tough as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the residue after burning, including cremated human remains.

clue.text: Width of river restricting vessels

indicators.note: restricting means the river's name holds the vessels inside

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A river's breadth confining boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats on the river, but here means cooking pots. The Exe is a river in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide stretch, an area of great breadth.

clue.text: Depression, a short minor illness

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a cold is a minor illness

explanation.surface: Feeling low, and also suffering a little bout of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood, but it is a dip in a ridge; 'short' drops the D of COLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a low pass or saddle between two mountain peaks, a depression in the ridge.

clue.text: An aphorism's coined for stroke management

indicators.note: coined means newly minted, so these letters are struck into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A clever saying has been invented about managing a stroke patient's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coined' rearranges AN APHORISM'S; 'stroke' is the rowing stroke, not a medical event.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill at rowing is about handling each pull of the oar, so it is the management of strokes.

clue.text: Mysterious vampire has been beheaded and buried by soldiers

indicators.note: buried by means the shortened word sits inside the soldiers' letters

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: beheaded means the word has lost its first letter

parts.note: Dracula is the famous vampire

explanation.surface: A gothic tale: the vampire is decapitated and soldiers inter him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been beheaded' removes the first letter of the vampire's name; 'buried by' then sets the rest between the soldiers' two letters. OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracular speech is like an oracle's, enigmatic and hard to interpret, hence mysterious.

clue.text: Small sort of stone endless problem for horse

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: paving is a kind of stone, as in paving stone

explanation.surface: A little stone without end causes trouble for a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts PAVING to PAVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spavin is a disease of a horse's hock joint, a bony swelling causing lameness.

clue.text: Diva carousing with sherry, briefly a way to suffer

indicators.note: carousing means drinking riotously, so the letters are thrown about
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: oloroso is a dark sweet sherry

explanation.surface: An opera star drinking sherry finds a road to misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carousing' turns DIVA into VIAD; 'briefly' shortens OLOROSO to OLOROS; then A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Via Dolorosa in Jerusalem is the route Christ walked to the crucifixion, literally the sorrowful way.

clue.text: Pelts round squares to achieve slender physique

indicators.note: round means the pelts word goes around the squares

parts.note: pelts are animal skins
nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: Wearing furs about the town square to look slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squares' looks like town squares or geometry, but means square numbers: nine is three squared.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thin, lean of build, is a slender physique.

clue.text: Housewife starts to experience trouble, unplugs iron

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A homemaker has a domestic mishap and pulls the plug on her iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housewife' is not a person here but an old word for a sewing case.
explanation.definitionFit: A housewife (pronounced 'hussif') is a small sewing kit, and an etui is a small needle case.

clue.text: Watch recording: sort of reception

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: Watching a recording of some kind of welcome party.
explanation.walkthrough: A ticker-tape reception is a parade where paper streamers are thrown from windows, a New York tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker-tape describes a celebratory welcome with paper showered on the honoured guests.

clue.text: Adjust one reason for enjoying a song

definitions.meaning: to make small precise changes to improve

definitions.text: one reason for enjoying a song
definitions.meaning: a good melody is a reason to like a song

explanation.surface: Changing something because it is one reason to like a song.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak precisely is the verb; split, it reads as a good melody.

clue.text: Chambers: "a representative collection"

definitions.meaning: the houses of a legislature, such as Commons and Lords
a gathering of elected representatives, and also the collective noun for owls

explanation.surface: Chambers, the dictionary publisher, quoted as describing something as a representative collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The legislature sits in chambers and is literally a body of assembled representatives.

clue.text: Skilled worker gets ideal job at the end of a few months

parts.note: a plum job is a highly desirable one

parts.words: the end of a few months
parts.note: September, October, November and December all end in the same three letters

explanation.surface: A tradesman lands his dream job after a few months.
explanation.walkthrough: BER ends four months of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber is a tradesperson who fits pipes, a skilled manual worker.

clue.text: Scowl and look embarrassed when company departs

indicators.note: departs means the company's letters leave the word

parts.note: to colour is to blush, to look embarrassed

explanation.surface: Someone frowns and blushes once their guests have left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departs' removes CO from COLOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour (or lower) is to frown or look sullen and threatening.

clue.text: Faith gets a new head — a prince, say

indicators.note: a new head means the first letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: loyalty is faithfulness

explanation.surface: A religion acquires a new leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets a new head' swaps the L of LOYALTY for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Princes are members of a royal family, examples of royalty.

clue.text: To succeed, I am everywhere.

parts.note: to pass a test is to succeed
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A boastful line: I'm a success wherever I go.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is Latin for here and there throughout, used in references.

clue.text: Lingerie is resurrected?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as ..., the reverse of dying, as if coming back to life

explanation.surface: A query whether some underwear has been brought back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is casual for underclothes; split as UN-DIES it playfully means reverses death.

clue.text: Threatening to trap military grouping in swampy surroundings

indicators.note: in places the alliance within the boggy word
surroundings confirms the boggy word wraps around the alliance

parts.note: miry means boggy, swampy
NATO is the North Atlantic military alliance

explanation.surface: A menace to catch an armed alliance in a marshy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to trap' is only a link here; the containment is signalled by 'in' and 'surroundings'.
explanation.definitionFit: Minatory is a formal adjective meaning menacing, expressing a threat.

clue.text: First to propose a way to save Italian city

indicators.note: First to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: an ISA, Individual Savings Account, is a UK tax-free savings scheme

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a rescue plan for the city.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is a Tuscan city, famed for its leaning tower.

clue.text: 27, for example, is grand affair

parts.note: big means grand
a business is an affair, a matter

explanation.surface: Something, presumably oil, is a grand affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across is OIL; the oil industry is an example of very large commercial enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Big business means large corporations, and the oil industry is a prime instance.

clue.text: Vehicle's performance: up and down

indicators.note: up and down means the word reads the same either way in this down entry

parts.note: a musical performance

explanation.surface: A car's performance has been uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: A gig is also a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a light horse-drawn carriage, a vehicle.

clue.text: Cat's back, but not tail, in picture

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read in reverse
not tail means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat's back, though not its tail, shown in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not tail' trims LION to LIO; 'back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil is a painting done in oil paints, so a picture.

clue.text: By 8th May 1945 almost fix sacred text

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the fixing word comes next to the shortened day

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: VE Day, Victory in Europe day, was 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: Trying to fix something by the end of the war in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims VE DAY to VEDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rig Veda is the oldest of the Hindu scriptures, a collection of Sanskrit hymns.

clue.text: Problem girl gives such offence?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, describing a type of offence

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A troublesome girl causes a certain kind of offence.
explanation.walkthrough: In English law a summary offence is a minor one tried by magistrates without a jury.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor crimes dealt with by magistrates are classed as summary offences.
